judgment.notes: The length-2*pi quotient and normalized measure match the original; the radius R is explicitly distinguished from the real field.
The integral coefficient, integer index, and distributional extension agree with the Fourier convention. Completion is with the Sobolev norms specified by D003.
The weighted completion, normalized L2, reality conjugation, and zero mode are explicit. The lost conjugation bar in plain extraction is resolved by the supplied checked transcription.
The homogeneous norm is restricted to mean-zero inputs. Both comparison inequalities, including the reversed factors for negative s, follow termwise from 1<=<k>/|k|<=sqrt(2).
The sign exp(i*t*k^3) matches exp(-t*partial_x^3); group composition and norm preservation follow directly from the multiplier, including on completions.
The zeroth distributional Fourier coefficient is a scalar identified with the corresponding constant function; no mean-zero assumption is introduced.
I-P0 defines precisely the complementary mean-zero projection; its dependency is D006.
The zero mode is explicitly assigned zero, so there is no division by zero. The nonzero multipliers give the stated one- and two-derivative gains since <k>/|k|<=sqrt(2).
The guarded tau>0, mean-zero L2 formula is exactly the fixed quadratic stage. Dinv f is H1, hence its square is well-defined and L2 (indeed H1) in one dimension.

All four terms, constants, signs, inverse derivatives, time arguments and endpoint subtraction match the original. For L2 inputs, Dinv f is H1, f^2 is L1, and the displayed smoothed products and mean exist; tau>0 guards 1/tau. No estimate or endpoint identity is assumed.

The unchanged Psi and finite recursion have the original grid, twisting and positive timestep guard. L2 products are defined by D009-D010; continuity and preservation are exported separately in N007 rather than assumed. No frequency cutoff is inserted.
The cutoff and complementary projection are defined for N>=0 on Fourier coefficients. They are explicitly proof/approximation devices, not part of Psi.
An integrable scalar time function and tau>0 suffice for the stated average; the divisor is guarded.
Both phase averages and their product are explicit with real phases and positive tau. Exponentials are integrable; no covariance estimate is granted by the definition.

The nonzero-output guard, omitted pair sum, phase identity, factor -tau/(18*i*k), and time phase exactly match (4). The polynomial core needs no convergence assumption; the smooth-input series is absolutely convergent by |eta|<=2 and rapidly decreasing coefficients. The rough bounded extension is correctly left to N004.
23/14 is a fixed positive rational, strictly greater than 3/2; it is not a new hypothesis on problem data.

The interval length, weak derivative codomain, essential suprema and X norm match the original. Continuous representatives are used only where continuity is supplied, not postulated for all L-infinity paths.
The twisted derivative-of-product defines B on smooth inputs and, for its actual L2 uses, on L1 products distributionally. The H^(-23/14) bound is an exported N005 conclusion, not a defining axiom.

The normal-form product has the correct two inverse derivatives and output projection. Actual uses are smooth inputs, L2 pairs, or A with Dinv A in L2 paired with an L2 input (N005); those products are legitimate using Dinv g in H1 subset L-infinity. No arbitrary product of distributions is required.

Both projections, the placement of the inverse derivative and time integral match the original. Initial smooth/piecewise smooth inputs make the construction legitimate; rough extensions are supplied by explicit estimates and sources, not hidden in D020.
The bilinear stage has factor 1/2, time-independent smooth mean-zero inputs and a<=t. The subsequent extension and bounds are separate conclusions.

Every component F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y is explicitly constructed for smooth data, with tau>0 and a>=0. D015 covers the smooth remainder. The linear endpoint correction has the exact sign and factor; endpoint matching and all estimates remain to be proved.

This specifies the original PDE, initial value, distributional meaning and smooth-approximation convention. Actual solution uses are C H^gamma with gamma>0, so u^2 is a distributionally meaningful L1 product. The definition explicitly grants neither existence nor a bound; N001 produces them.
